body.statement: For a partially directed acyclic graph on \(p\) vertices and \(m\) edges, there is an algorithm that enumerates every consistent directed-acyclic extension exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization, with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay.

source.verbatim_statement: There is an algorithm that enumerates all consistent extensions of a given PDAG with linear-time delay after an initialization step of time \(O(n^{3})\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem 5; Algorithm 7 supplies exact consistent-extension enumeration, and the paper's linear-delay analysis is O(vertices plus edges).

body.justification: This published algorithm supplies only the extension-enumeration complexity used after the local canonical-lift theorem.
body.gap: The cited theorem enumerates PDAG extensions but has no coefficient-block state or partition-lift statement.
body.consumer: The canonical-lift proposition transfers the algorithm to blocked covariance-equivalence components.
